audit.why: The shape is right: Tryndamere owns 1 through 5 because every one of his abilities costs zero resource and is limited only by cooldown, level 6 is the flip to Skill because Riftwalk finally answers Spinning Slash, and he reclaims the item stages on crit scaling and splitpush. Sides and ratings left untouched.

audit.whatIsWrong: Undying Rage is called 'the clock this lane runs on' in five places and its cooldown is never once given.
audit.why: It is 120/100/80 seconds. That is the single largest number in the matchup and it is what makes the advice actionable: at rank 1 a spent Undying Rage buys you two full minutes in which Tryndamere is a normal champion with no escape from a blink assassin. 'Wait for its cooldown' without the number is a mood; '120 seconds at rank 1' is a plan. It also reframes his spike timing — he does not get a reliable second R in a laning phase.
audit.corrected: Undying Rage: 120s at rank 1, 100s at 2, 80s at 3, 400 range. One spent R at level 6 is a two-minute window where he cannot survive your burst.

audit.whatIsWrong: Mocking Shout is written as a flat slow you must blink out of ('blink out of his E gap-close or W slow'), with no mention of its condition.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Tryndamere lets out an insulting cry, decreasing surrounding champions' Attack Damage. Enemies with their backs turned to Tryndamere also have their Move Speed reduced.' The slow is conditional on facing away. Against Kassadin that is the whole point — Mocking Shout punishes running, and Riftwalk is instant, so the correct response is to blink rather than walk. Written as an unconditional slow it teaches you to fear a debuff that, if you never turn your back, is only an AD reduction on a champion whose AD you were not worried about. 14s cooldown, 850 range.
audit.corrected: Mocking Shout only slows enemies with their backs turned. Blink out with Riftwalk instead of walking out and it is just an AD debuff.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spinning Slash is treated as a free gap-close with no cooldown number and no cast condition.
audit.why: Riot's text is 'Tryndamere slices toward a target unit' — it requires a unit to slice toward, and it is 12/11/10/9/8 seconds at 650 range. Both halves are actionable for a champion with no escape until 6: the wave state controls whether he can reach you at all, so a thin or dead wave is a shorter leash, and 12 seconds at rank 1 is a real gap you can walk up in. Neither number nor condition appears anywhere on the page.
audit.corrected: Spinning Slash is 12s at rank 1, 650 range, and it needs a target unit to travel to — deny him minions between you and you deny the dash.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'hold Null Sphere to chunk and interrupt him when he overcommits' in the early text, and 'Q-silence the counterplay' in breakdown.late.
audit.why: Null Sphere 'interrupts channels' — Tryndamere has no channelled ability in his kit, so there is nothing here for the interrupt to catch and the advice sends you looking for a cast that never comes. And Null Sphere has never silenced in this kit version; the shield half is the part that matters, and against a pure-physical champion even that is the wrong tool. Both lines promise a defensive button Kassadin does not have in this specific matchup.
audit.corrected: Null Sphere against Tryndamere is damage and a magic shield only — there is no channel to interrupt and it has never silenced.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tryndamere.json (no channel flag on any ability)

audit.why: 'Void Stone's magic damage reduction is dead weight versus his physical crit' is right and correctly stated in three places — his entire kit is physical, and the Null Sphere shield absorbs magic only. That is the honest framing and I kept it.
'Add anti-heal early into his sustain' is already in Itemization, which covers the flagged needs-antiheal interaction (Bloodlust consumes Fury to heal, 12s cooldown, free to cast). Nothing to add.
50.00% over 14 games; the page quotes no figure. No change.

edits.before: Forget Void Stone's 15% magic damage reduction this lane — Tryndamere is pure physical crit, so your passive does nothing for his trades. Level 1 is roughly a wash since you both just want farm, but at 2-3 he can E-slash onto you with no escape on your side, and your Null Sphere shield only absorbs magic, not his autos. Last-hit at max Q range, hold Null Sphere to chunk and interrupt him when he overcommits, and never fight while his Fury bar is high.
edits.after: Forget Void Stone's 15% magic damage reduction this lane — Tryndamere is pure physical crit, so your passive is dead weight in his trades. Level 1 is roughly a wash since you both just want farm, but at 2-3 Spinning Slash (12s at rank 1) carries him onto you, and your Null Sphere shield absorbs magic only, never his autos. It needs a target unit to travel to, so a thin wave is a shorter leash — last-hit at max Q range and never fight a full Fury bar.

edits.before: Once your stall item is up and Riftwalk is maxed, you blink faster than he can E-chase and you finally apply pressure instead of just eating it. But respect Undying Rage — your blink burst won't kill him through five seconds of immortality, so don't dump Riftwalk stacks into a fresh R and get spun down after it ends. Late game he becomes a splitpush problem: you want to be blinking onto squishies in fights while your team answers his side lane, not dueling him 1v1 into his crit and Undying Rage.
edits.after: Once your stall item is up and Riftwalk is maxed, you blink faster than he can E-chase and you finally apply pressure instead of just eating it. But respect Undying Rage — 120s at rank 1 down to 80s at rank 3, and your blink burst cannot kill through it, so never dump Riftwalk stacks into a fresh one and get spun down when it ends. Late he is a splitpush problem: blink onto squishies in fights while your team answers his side lane, rather than dueling his crit 1v1.

edits.after: Riftwalk answers Spinning Slash (12s at rank 1), and Mocking Shout only slows a turned back — blink out rather than run and his all-in stops being free.

notes: Two numbers on this page are not in Riot's text and I left them alone rather than swap one guess for another: 'five seconds' of Undying Rage (Riot says only 'unable to die, no matter how wounded' — no duration published) and 'survives your burst at 1 HP' in whys[6] (Riot publishes no minimum-HP figure). Both are listed in unverified. Where I rewrote around them I used 'while it runs' instead of asserting a duration. Also, the repo-wide 'Q-silence' boilerplate in breakdown.late is present here too.
